topPRs.title: op-reth: keep proofs history shard keys valid on unwind
topPRs.author: akatsukiwork0320
topPRs.body:
Unwinding proofs history could leave the surviving boundary shard under its old key. After new appends, historical reads could fall through to current state, making `eth_getProof` serve chain-tip trie nodes for historical blocks, as reported in #22501.

Unwind now walks backwards from each key's actual last shard and restores the surviving tail under `u64::MAX`. This preserves the sentinel expected by appends, including when an earlier version left a tail without one. Re-keying to the surviving maximum would fix the lookup but leave the append invariant broken. Retention pruning is unchanged.

This prevents the reported stale-key defect during subsequent unwinds; it is not a migration of previously corrupted history. Untouched malformed intermediate shards can still produce incorrect historical proofs and need separate recovery.

Local validation: `just lint` passed. `just test-unit`, restricted to the changed crate and its reverse dependency closure (17 of 76 workspace packages), passed with 822 tests and 3 skipped. Online tests were excluded; no live-chain/RPC proof replay was performed. Regression tests cover table round trips, boundary-shard structure, legacy finite tails and neighbouring keys. An equivalent AI review against the `rust-code-reviewer` guide found no blocking issues; no findings were dismissed.

Root-cause analysis and original reproduction by @omerfirmak.
Closes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/22501

Prepared with AI assistance, including implementation, tests and local validation.
